event.name: Slush 2026
event.participation_evidence: Platform directory/profile evidence, public event announcements, and supplied company-profile statements are distinguished per record. Physical attendance has not been independently verified.

limitations: The People directory is evidence of platform membership, not independently verified physical attendance.
Directory result totals may be capped; no assertion is made that every event attendee is represented.
A full profile text capture can still lack destinations of social-media icon buttons.
Missing values mean not captured or not displayed; they are not asserted to be absent from the person's background.
Location wording is preserved exactly as displayed, including apparent inconsistencies.
Company name matching supplies company metadata and does not independently verify the person's current employment.
Directory records without an exposed person UUID retain a local record_key and null platform ID/profile URL.
Directory-to-profile enrichment uses a unique exact displayed name, or an exact name and avatar; the matching method is recorded.
A +N tag indicator is preserved as tag_overflow_count; hidden tag values have not been invented.
The uploaded company file contains named attendees for 137 of 6275 companies. Companies with empty attendee arrays do not supply identities and do not imply zero attendance.
Imported people retain their supplied attendance statuses and original sources. General professional biographies do not independently establish event participation.
The upgraded primary collection includes one unresolved possible duplicate pair named Ben Fletcher. It is a record count, not a guaranteed unique-human count.
The source file repeats Simon Schaefer under two companies. One person record retains both sourced affiliations.
Public-source research may be partial or inaccessible; unknown fields remain empty, and full work or education histories are not asserted.
Platform directory coverage remains 744 entries with 10 full profile captures. Adding outside evidence does not reduce the count of uncaptured directory entries.

company_catalog.role: Company metadata only; does not establish any person's attendance.

export_metadata.incomplete_reason: Interactive directory pagination and profile collection were interrupted by repeated connected-browser timeouts. The observed bulk data response could not be acquired through the supported browser download interface.
export_metadata.possible_directory_result_cap_note: The unfiltered People UI displayed 10000 results. This figure was not verified as the total registered attendee count or as an uncapped directory total.
export_metadata.avatar_reference_note: Image URLs are stored without temporary signing query parameters. They identify observed image resources but may require authorization and are not guaranteed to be publicly downloadable.

data_semantics.people: One primary record per resolved person or unresolved identity candidate from the platform captures and supplied named-attendee evidence. Source types distinguish the 744 captured directory entries from imported people; one possible Ben Fletcher duplicate is retained explicitly.
data_semantics.existing_attendance_evidence: Unchanged original 210 evidence rows, now linked to 209 primary person records. These are audit evidence, not additional people or new platform captures.
data_semantics.null_values: Unknown or unverified scalar values are null; missing collections use empty arrays or retain the baseline null value. An empty value does not assert that the underlying information does not exist.
data_semantics.local_record_keys: Export-local identifiers only; not Slush platform person IDs.
data_semantics.section_present: For work_experience, education and social_media, section_present records whether a platform section was captured. External entries can exist while section_present is false; their provenance identifies the public source.
data_semantics.affiliations: Company-specific roles from the supplied attendee records. Company headquarters remain exclusively in linked_company_metadata.
data_semantics.public_source_job_title: Title read from current public research. Existing captured platform titles remain unchanged; differing source wording is preserved.
data_semantics.employment_dates: An organization joining year does not establish the start of a current senior title. organization_join_year and organization_join_date preserve such dates separately; entries with date_semantics=organization_join_date explicitly date the affiliation only. A null end_date means not verified and does not by itself imply current employment.

observed_bulk_source.discovery: Resource observed in the People directory page asset inventory.

export_metadata.completion_input_needed: A supported full attendee/profile export or saved People directory response JSON. A card-projection response may resolve the roster and IDs, but additional profile data may still be needed for work history, education and social destinations.

official_visibility_reference.note: Slush permits attendees to make their profile not visible, so even a complete visible-directory export does not prove coverage of every registered attendee.

last_upgrade.unknown_field_policy: null for unknown scalar fields; [] for newly introduced missing collections. No guessed identities, titles, locations, links, work entries or education.
last_upgrade.matching_policy: Name alone is insufficient. Sauraj Gambhir is merged using exact name plus explicit Prior Labs affiliation in the captured biography. Simon Schaefer is combined using the same official person URL. Ben Fletcher remains a possible duplicate.

people.biography: An incoming business student at Aalto University, volunteering at Slush this year to see the startup world up close before my studies begin. I’m curious about how founders turn an idea into a company, what investors look for, and what it’s actually like to work at an early-stage startup. It feels like a special moment to be starting out while AI is changing how companies are built, how small teams can be, and what a business degree even prepares you for. I’d love to hear the stories behind what you’re building, the mistakes you learned the most from, and any advice for someone just starting out. Always happy to chat over coffee between sessions :)

people.biography: I’m Hridoy Chowdhury — a Software Engineer, entrepreneur, and CS Master’s student based in Helsinki. I’ve spent 3+ years building mobile apps in Swift, Kotlin, and AI-powered pipelines, including large-audience apps with over 2M users. My experience spans iOS development, cross-platform engineering, ML workflows, and rapid prototyping of consumer AI products. I currently lead the Innovation & Development Unit at IntexResearch Lab, where I focus on turning ideas into real, usable software — from AI transcription & summarization tools to AI-powered note-generation and study assistants. I’m also the co-founder of JoyNow, an activity-matching platform backed by the University of Helsinki’s Pre-Incubator Program, helping people find partners and communities to enjoy sports and shared activities together. I love building things that make people’s lives easier — fast, intuitive, AI-native products that scale.

linked_company_metadata.company_description:
NeuroHarmonics has built a way to write to the deep human brain without surgery.

The circuits that govern movement, mood, pain and motivation sit deep in the brain. Acting on them directly is one of the most powerful things medicine can do. An electrode in the right few millimetres can quiet a tremor in seconds, but placing it takes neurosurgery, so it reaches almost no one.

Our system reaches the same circuits from outside the head. A person sits in a chair, and within minutes focused ultrasound is acting on a target a few millimetres wide, deep in their brain. Our first patient trial, in essential tremor, is open at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London.

The target and dose are set in software, so we can act on a circuit, measure the response and adjust, session after session. We are starting with tremor, and plan to expand to depression, chronic pain and addiction. Our long-term ambition is a world model of the human brain, learned by acting on it.

Conductor Quantum is building quantum superintelligence: AI that operates quantum computers to make scientific discoveries beyond human reach.

Quantum computers let us understand the world at its most fundamental level, the path to new drugs, new materials, and discoveries no human can reach alone.

A quantum computer is the perfect simulator of nature: it encodes the logic of reality into a programmable machine, atom by atom, electron by electron. Give AI that simulator and you open the door to discovery.

The bottleneck is operating the hardware. Today, engineers spend days or weeks by hand to bring a chip to operating conditions for just two qubits. A qubit is the information-carrying unit of a quantum computer, the equivalent of a bit in a classical one, and a useful machine needs billions.

We build the AI that operates quantum computers and tunes every machine it runs on. That is the path to quantum superintelligence.

Our technology combines (i) the world's largest dataset of literature-extracted experimental data, (ii) predictive models trained on it, (iii) high-throughput quantum simulation workflows, (iv) ML models that predict simulation outcomes, and (v) generative models that explore the full chemical space to find materials with target properties. 

We apply this technology to atomic-scale deposition and etching: discovering new ALD precursors, modeling processes through digital twins, and designing thin films, with first use cases in semiconductors, batteries and catalysis.

The platform shortens R&D cycles by several orders of magnitude versus traditional empirical approaches, enabling advanced chips.

linked_company_metadata.company_description:
Valla builds legal technology for people navigating disputes without a lawyer, and for the courts and legal professionals managing those disputes at scale.
On the consumer side, Valla guides self-represented litigants through their case: assessing the merits, preparing documents, tracking deadlines, and connecting them to real legal expertise when they need it. It's not a generic document generator — the product is built by practising barristers working alongside engineers, so the guidance reflects genuine legal judgment, not just templated forms.
On the institutional side, Valla gives courts and lawyers the infrastructure to handle a caseload that's growing faster than the system can process, including the emerging wave of AI-generated filings.
We started with UK employment disputes, where tribunal backlogs are at record highs, and we're building toward other dispute types and markets from there.
